description:
ActivationSymbol (src/compiler2/transport.rs) stores a boxed copy of its arrow's parameter list. Identity ignores it (fz-53f.6), and production reads it in one place: the telemetry writer (src/telemetry/jsonl.rs write_activation_symbol), which prints it as the "input" array beside the arrow. Every clone of an ActivationSymbol / ExecutableSymbol / TransportPosition copies the box.

Measured on develop ac3750d1e plus the fz-sc8.95 hasher fix (532f77b88): transport.rs:211 (the derived Clone) is 106,672 of 969,355 allocations on the OptionParser probe. Spike (field removed, telemetry no longer writes "input"): 857,327 allocations, program output and canonical backend dump identical.

Change: remove the field, ActivationSymbol::new and input(); the symbol is {function, arrow} and Copy with derived Eq/Hash. Telemetry writes function and arrow; the parameter list is a function of the arrow, which the type table on the stream already resolves. Tests that read input() read types.arrow_params(&arrow); tests that pin the list being shared by pointer go with the list. .agent/docs/telemetry.md states the arrow field alone.

Signal: full gate green; no golden, census or pin rises; probe output and canon identical; allocation count before and after in the commit.
title: An activation symbol is its function and arrow, and carries no parameter list
